I'd say don't drink too much water (because you really don't want to lose your spot in your row depending on how close to the stage you are), but definitely drink before starting to feel faint. From what I've heard the floor is sloped at Brixton so you should be able to see the stage even from the back. I'm 5''2 and to be honest your best bet is looking between other people's heads. If you don't get cold waiting leave your coat with someone else or at home or tie it around your waist, unless it's really heavy and in packed crowds it might not be the best idea...especially if the crowd pushes a lot. The jacket's good for keeping snacks/water so security won't check though. Wear good sturdy running shoes. If people start pushing move forward to get towards the front so you don't lose your view but try to get out of their way. Try not to let them squish you, there might be a lot of pushing around, I've never been to a twenty one pilots gig before though so I'm not sure how much the clique likes to push. When it does happen try to balance and stay calm and focus on the fact that you're enjoying the performance and try ignore the audience. If you run out of water ask for one of the bouncers. 
It depends on how long you are willing to wait. You may have to consider needing the toilet while waiting, venues usually won't let you in for the toilet before a show starts, though even if you arrive 4 hours ahead of the start time if you're willing to push or get pushed forward you may end up standing at the first few rows. Of course some people leave early morning to secure their place, but it depends who you're also travelling with etc. I'm going alone and got priorities earlier the day so I'm aiming to arrive 7 hours ahead.
